match.description: The criteria a captured span must satisfy. 'traceId' is REQUIRED — this family asserts the causal chain of a SPECIFIC transaction, not a general shape any span might match; service/spanName/attributes are optional refinements layered on top of it.

traceId.description: Required expected trace id — ties this assertion to the SPECIFIC transaction under test (never omit it: a match with no trace id would accept any span with the right service/spanName/attributes, from any trace, ever exported). May be a full W3C traceparent value (the 32-hex trace-id segment is extracted automatically) or a bare 32-hex trace id. May contain {placeholder} and ${secret:source/path} tokens.

service.description: Optional expected exporting-resource service name (the span's resource-level service.name attribute). May contain {placeholder} and ${secret:source/path} tokens.

spanName.description: Optional expected span name (operation name). May contain {placeholder} and ${secret:source/path} tokens.

attributes.description: Optional map of expected span-attribute key to expected value, compared as text (subset match — the real span may carry additional attributes not mentioned here) — a bare numeric or boolean scalar is read as its literal text. Each value may contain {placeholder} and ${secret:source/path} tokens.

then.description: Asserts that a captured inbound HTTP request against a host-owned webhook listener matches the declared criteria (method, path, headers, and/or body substring).

listener.description: Logical name of the host-owned webhook listener whose captured inbound requests this step asserts against.  The engine stands the listener up and stages its URL at svc::<listener> (and at the plain <listener> Vars key so an earlier step can interpolate {<listener>}).

match.description: The criteria a captured inbound request must satisfy.  At least one criterion (method, path, headers, or bodyContains) must be declared.

method.description: Optional expected HTTP method (case-insensitive equality).  May contain {placeholder} and ${secret:source/path} tokens.

path.description: Optional expected request path (the token-stripped, SUT-facing path; ordinal equality).  May contain {placeholder} and ${secret:source/path} tokens.

headers.description: Optional map of expected header names to their expected values, compared as text — a bare numeric or boolean scalar is read as its literal text.

bodyContains.description: Optional substring the captured request body must contain (ordinal).  May contain {placeholder} and ${secret:source/path} tokens. May be written as a bare number/boolean scalar; it is matched as text either way.

captureEntry.description: The value of a single 'capture' entry (DSL §6.1): either a bare scalar JSONPath expression (back-compat default — accepts ANY YamlDotNet scalar, not only a string, e.g. 'bad: 42', so this schema accepts every scalar shape the engine does, mirroring 'env'/'httpPort'/seed's 'sql' entries), or a single-key mapping naming the extractor format explicitly — '{ jsonpath: "$.id" }' or '{ xpath: "//id" }'. Exactly one of 'jsonpath'/'xpath' is required in the mapping form — neither, or both, is rejected.
captureEntry.$comment: ParseCaptureEntry's bare-scalar branch is the reader the description above generalises from: it accepts ANY YamlDotNet scalar, not only a string. 'minProperties: 1' below rejects neither (safe: 'additionalProperties: false' already confines keys to 'jsonpath'/'xpath', and 'minProperties' is a no-op against the bare-scalar form — JSON Schema draft 2020-12 §6.5.1), and the 'allOf'/'if'/'then' clause rejects both (mirrors $defs/service's own image/project mutual-exclusion pattern — see that definition's remarks for why a per-field boolean 'false' subschema is used rather than a second discriminating branch). A single 'type' union plus 'minProperties', not a top-level 'anyOf' discriminating string-vs-object, on purpose: the previous 'anyOf: [{required:[jsonpath]},{required:[xpath]}]' produced the SAME composite-branch noise a 'oneOf' does elsewhere in this schema — JsonSchema.Net 9.2.1's List-format output surfaces a non-matching anyOf branch's own failing keyword even when the OTHER branch made the anyOf as a whole valid. 'minProperties'/'properties'/'additionalProperties' are all no-ops against a non-object instance (JSON Schema draft 2020-12 §6.3.3/§6.5.1/§6.5.3), so the object-only rules below apply cleanly to the bare-scalar form with zero spurious evaluation. Accepted trade (mirrors the identical widening for 'env'/'httpPort'/seed's 'sql'): a non-string, non-JSONPath-syntax bare scalar (e.g. 'bad: 42') is schema-valid here yet still fails at RUNTIME once JSONPath evaluation rejects '42' as a malformed expression — the parser-parity principle (this schema accepts exactly what YamlDocumentParser accepts) takes precedence over pre-empting every possible downstream runtime failure; no behaviour change from that principle already being applied elsewhere.

jsonpath.description: A JSONPath expression evaluated against the step's result as JSON.

xpath.description: An XPath expression evaluated against the step's result as XML.
